thread:
nina: CobaltAI flagged INV-8320 — they say SLA credit for Nov latency breach wasn't applied. They claim ~1hr of degraded service and expect the 10% monthly credit.

clare: Invoice shows no SLA credit line. Do we have the incident window and how SLA calc ran?

paul: pulling SLA calc. sla-bot output attached: `SLA_REPORT INV-8320: total_degraded_minutes=59.4, credit_percent=0.0 (threshold rounding to hours)`

sla-bot: SLA engine note: credit applied only when degraded_minutes >= 60 (rounding to nearest hour). Current policy used integer hours for computation.

nina: CobaltAI insists the platform was degraded for 59.4 mins — that's within rounding error and they want the credit. They are an enterprise customer on Dedicated with a strict SLO.

clare: Finance perspective: policy is clear but for enterprise goodwill and to avoid churn we can approve a one-time pro-rated credit. Need amount calc and journal guidance.

paul: If we prorate by minutes, 10% monthly credit on reserved commit ($72,000/mo) for 59.4/ (30*24*60) ~= 0.0138% of monthly charge. That comes to ~ $10 — negligible. But customer expected 10% because they assumed the SLA is binary for hour blocks.

nina: hmm customer emailed escalation and asked for full 10% on reserved commit line, arguing the breach impacted heavy batch jobs. They also threatened to push procurement hold.

clare: Given risk, recommend offering a goodwill credit of 10% on a single day's reserved-commit pro rata instead of full month. Approve up to $1,500. We'll flag as one-off.

paul: OK I'll prepare journal. Recommended credit: 10% of one day of reserved commit. Calculation: monthly $72,000 / 30 = $2,400 per day, 10% = $240. Approve to issue $240 credit.

nina: that's reasonable. I'll tell CobaltAI AP and avoid escalation. Also request engineering patch to SLA calc.

ops-bot: Ticket OPENED -> SRE-1142: Change SLA engine to compute credits based on minutes and accept fractional-hour windows. Assigned to @paul_ops. Priority P2.

paul: I'll also add an alert when degraded_minutes is within 2 minutes of threshold so we can proactively review.

billing-bot: Created credit memo CR-8320-GW amount $240 status PENDING_APPROVAL. Use `billing-cli credits approve --id CR-8320-GW` to finalize. Export: /exports/credits/CR-8320-GW.json

clare: Finance approves $240 goodwill credit. Post GL memo: "Goodwill SLA credit CR-8320-GW issued to CobaltAI for fractional-hour SLA breach; one-off; no policy precedence."

nina: Sent customer note: apologised, issued $240 credit, promised SLA engine fix and monitoring change. They accepted and will proceed with payment. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
